items.title: What do employers usually look at in recruitment?

values: Materials｜entirely fictional｜45 minutes of paper preparation
Design a 20-minute micro-lesson on "mean, median and extreme values" for the 30 fictional university students in course U; do not actually teach and do not use real grades.
Prerequisites: integer addition and division. The only data are the five values 2, 3, 3, 4, 18; the mean is the sum divided by the count, and the median is the middle value after sorting.
Assignment A: calculate the mean and median of the original data and explain why they differ. Assignment B: change 18 to 8, recalculate both values and explain the effect of the extreme value.

Fictional sample A: response A gives mean 6, median 3, and says 18 pulls the mean up; response B gives mean 4, median 3, and says the mean falls after the change while the median does not. Fictional sample B: response A gives mean 30 and median 18, reasoning that the maximum is most representative; response B gives mean 20 and median 8, writing that both measures fall because the maximum gets smaller.
Task and deliverable｜work independently first

45 minutes: the first 10 minutes to write two observable objectives, then 15 minutes to write a 20-minute teaching plan, then 15 minutes to grade A and B against the same rubric, and the last 5 minutes to give B feedback and revise one teaching activity.

Deliverable 1: the objectives and the 20-minute activity; deliverable 2: the four-dimension 8-point rubric, A and B scores and the basis; deliverable 3: one specific error, the next practice step and one reason for changing the lesson.

Four dimensions scored 0–2 each: the mean of the original data, the median of the original data, the mean and median after replacement, and the explanation of the change. 2 points means all correct with a basis; 1 point means the method or a key part is right but incomplete; 0 points means wrong or missing. The total is 8 points and is used only for this exercise.
Reference answer｜look only after completing

Objective one: can correctly calculate the mean and median of five numbers and show the process. Objective two: can compare the two measures after replacing an extreme value and explain the difference.

20 minutes: 0–3 minutes diagnose "does the maximum equal the median"; 3–8 minutes demonstrate sorting and summing; 8–13 minutes complete A independently and check answers; 13–18 minutes complete B and discuss in pairs; 18–20 minutes write a one-sentence exit explanation.
A: sum 30, mean 30/5=6, median 3; B: sum 20, mean 20/5=4, median 3. The change in the extreme value lowers the mean by 2 while the median is unchanged.

Sample A scores 2 on all four dimensions, 8/8 in total; sample B scores 0 on the first two dimensions and 0 on the third, and 1 point on the fourth for identifying that the extreme value got smaller but wrongly saying the median falls with it, 1/8 in total. Neither the sums 30 or 20 may be treated as the mean, nor the maximum as the median.

Feedback for B: "You noticed the extreme value got smaller, which is a correct observation. First sort the five numbers and circle the third, then divide the sum by 5; rewrite why the median is still 3." Lesson change: add a demonstration comparing sorting to find the middle number with dividing the sum by the count.
Boundaries and review

The 45 paper minutes are preparation time and the 20 minutes is the proposed teaching length; the two times are not added together to imply actual classroom time. The 30 students are a fictional setting, and only samples A and B can be graded.
The rubric, samples, scores and lesson change are editorial exercises; they do not represent university standards, formal grading authority, student performance or hiring.

subject.name: Postsecondary Teachers
subject.summary: Postsecondary teachers teach subject courses, design syllabi, assignments and assessments and advise students at higher education institutions such as universities, colleges and community colleges; some positions also conduct research, publish and take part in departmental service. The specific balance of teaching and research varies with the school, subject and appointment type. The US wages and employment on this page use the BLS Postsecondary Teachers aggregate page; O*NET 25-1081 is only a task sample for education teachers.
